title: Commitment Pricing Slate and Governance Checklist for Enterprise Billing Requests
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customer account teams frequently submit ad-hoc pricing and commitment requests (discounts, invoice crediting, marketplace offsets) with inconsistent information. This causes long turnaround, risk of revenue leakage, and disagreement between sales, finance, and legal.

Goal: Produce a standardized evaluation ‘slate’ and lightweight governance checklist that triages incoming non-bug billing requests into clear buckets (auto-approve, PM review, finance approval required, legal review). The slate should make trade-offs visible (unit economics, SLA/product risk, operational overhead) and provide an escalation flow so requests are handled consistently and auditable.

Deliverables: 1) a one-page Commitment Pricing Slate template used by sales/AMs; 2) a governance checklist for PM/Finance/Legal reviewers; 3) an annotated decision matrix for triage; 4) Slack + Drive templates and a short rollout doc for GTM teams.
acceptance_criteria: A sales/AM can complete the Commitment Pricing Slate in under 10 minutes with the information we require
Triage outcomes map to a specific next step (auto-approve, needs PM signoff, needs finance signoff, needs legal review)
At least two pilot enterprise requests processed using the slate end-to-end with documented time-to-decision and reviewer notes
Governance checklist includes clear thresholds for revenue impact, contract length, and marketplace offsets
Stakeholders (Sales Ops, Finance, Legal, PM) sign off on the checklist and escalation paths
decision_matrix: Revenue impact (ARR or one-time credit) — primary axis
Implementation complexity (billing systems / invoicing adjustments) — secondary axis
Programmatically enforceable? (can be handled by policy or requires manual review)
Risk vector (data residency, regulatory, security, contractual change)
escalation_path: Auto-approve: request meets policy thresholds and finance policy flags = none
PM review: changes to product entitlements, non-standard SLAs, or > $X MRR impact
Finance review: invoicing adjustments, credits > $Y, deferred revenue implications
Legal review: contract amendments, indemnities, or changes to data residency clauses
Executive review (CRO/CFO): strategic exceptions or > $Z multi-year commitments
